questions.question: The marked price of an article is 160 percent of the cost price. If 20 percent discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 160% of Cost Price (CP)

Discount = 20% of MP

Find Profit Percentage

**Concept:**

Profit or Loss is calculated on CP.

**Solution:**

Let the CP = 100 (For simplicity)

Hence, MP = 160 (As MP is 160% of CP)

Discount = 20% of MP = 20% of 160 = 32

Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount = 160 - 32 = 128

Profit = SP - CP = 128 - 100 = 28

Profit Percentage = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (28/100) × 100 = 28%

**Hence, the profit percentage is 28% (Option 1).**

questions.question: The Largest possible sphere is carved from a cube of side 6 cm. What is the volume of the sphere?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cube Side = 6 cm

Find volume of largest sphere

**Concept:**

The diameter of the sphere is equal to the side of the cube. Volume of sphere = 4/3 π r³.

**Solution:**

Radius (r) of sphere = Cube side/2 = 6/2 = 3 cm

Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × r³ = 4/3 × π × (3)³

Volume of sphere = 4/3 × π × 27 = 36π cm³

Value of π = 22/7

Volume of sphere = 36 × 22/7 = 792/7 cm³

**Hence, the volume of the sphere is 792/7 cm³ (Option 1).**

questions.question: Working 15 hours a day, Vaibhav can complete a piece of work in 35 days. How many hours a day should he work so as finish the work in 25 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 35 × 15 = 525 hours

Required hours per day = Total work ÷ New number of days

Required hours per day = 525 ÷ 25 = 21 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 21 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ In Case 1, Vaibhav works 15 hours per day to achieve a daily efficiency of 5 units.

⇒ Work done per hour = 5 ÷ 15 = 1/3 units/hour

⇒ In Case 2, Vaibhav's required daily efficiency is 7 units.

⇒ Number of hours required per day = Required daily efficiency ÷ Work done per hour

⇒ Hours per day = 7 ÷ (1/3)

⇒ Hours per day = 7 × 3 = 21 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Formula)

The general formula for time and work is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M is men, D is days, H is hours, and W is work.

Inverse Proportion

When the total work remains constant, the number of days taken is inversely proportional to the number of hours worked per day (i.e., more hours per day means fewer days required).

questions.question: Find the value of 62.5 × 2 + 1100 - (16)² + (30)² :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Evaluate powers and products simultaneously to save time:

⇒ 62.5 × 2 = 125, (16)² = 256, (30)² = 900

⇒ 125 + 1100 − 256 + 900

⇒ 1225 + 644

⇒ 1869

**∴ The correct answer is 1869.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

62.5 × 2 + 1100 − (16)² + (30)²

**Formula Used:**

BODMAS Rule: Brackets, Orders (Powers/Roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 62.5 × 2 + 1100 − (16)² + (30)²

⇒ 62.5 × 2 + 1100 − 256 + 900

⇒ 125 + 1100 − 256 + 900

⇒ 1225 − 256 + 900

⇒ 969 + 900

⇒ 1869

**∴ The correct answer is 1869.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the correct sequence to solve mathematical expressions: Brackets, Orders (powers and roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Squares and Cubes

Memorizing squares of numbers up to 30 and cubes up to 15 is highly beneficial for quickly evaluating the Orders part in simplification problems.

Decimal Multiplication

When multiplying decimals by a whole number, treat them as integers first and place the decimal point in the product so that it has the same number of decimal places as the original decimal number.
</p

questions.question: The average age of 15 members of a committee is increased by 4 years when two members whose ages are 60 years and 70 years are replaced by the two new members. What is the average age of the new members?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Average age of 15 members increased by 4 years when two members of ages 60 and 70 are replaced

**Concept: **

Average is the sum of all observations divided by the number of observations.

**Solution:**

Total increase in age = 15 members × 4 years/member = 60 years

Sum of ages of new members = Sum of ages of replaced members + Total increase in age = 60 + 70 + 60 = 190 years

Average age of new members = Sum of ages of new members/Number of new members = 190/2 = 95 years

**Hence, the average age of the new members is 95 years (Option 4).**

questions.question: The ratio of ages of two students is 5 ∶ 4. The difference between their ages is 8 years. What is the age of the younger student?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Age ratio = 5 ∶ 4

Age difference = 8 years

Find younger student's age

**Concept: **

Ratio of two quantities of the same kind and in the same units is a fraction that shows how many times the one quantity is of the other.

**Solution:**

Difference in ratio = 5 - 4 = 1

Age corresponding to 1 part in ratio = Age difference = 8 years

Younger student's age = 4 parts in ratio × Age corresponding to 1 part in ratio = 4 × 8 = 32 years

**Hence, the age of the younger student is 32 years (Option 2).**

questions.question: If A can do a work in 21 days and B can do the same work in 28 days. In how many days will they complete the work if they work on alternate days?
questions.solution:
A's work time = 21 days

B's work time = 28 days

Find time to complete work if A and B work alternately

**Concept: **Work done is inversely proportional to time taken. If they work on alternate days, their work done adds up.

**Solution:**

A's work/day = 1/21

B's work/day = 1/28

Work done by A and B in 2 days = 1/21 + 1/28 = 4/84 + 3/84 = 7/84

Time taken for 1 complete work = 2 × 84/7 = 24 days

**Hence, they will complete the work in 24 days.**

questions.question: On certain sum, the simple interest for 2 years is Rs. 12000. If the sum is Rs. 12000, then what will be the compound interest (compounding annually) on the same sum at the same rate of interest for the first 3 years?
questions.solution:
Principal (P) = Rs. 12000

Simple interest (SI) for 2 years = Rs. 12000

Find compound interest (CI) for 3 years

Concept: Rate of interest can be calculated from SI, then applied to calculate CI.

Solution:

Rate of interest (r) = (SI × 100)/(P × t) = (12000 × 100)/(12000 × 2) = 50% per annum

CI for 3 years at 50% per annum = P[(1 + r/100)3 - 1] = 12000[(1 + 50/100)3 - 1]

CI = 12000[(3/2)3 - 1] = 12000[27/8 - 1] = Rs. 28500

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Interest = 12000 for 2 years

So 

Interest = 6000 for 1 year

Principal = Rs. 12000

Means Rate of Interest = 50%

So

Compound interest for 3 years:-

Compound interest for 2 years = 50 + 50 + 50 × 50/100 = 125%

Compound interest for 3 years = 125 + 50 + 125 × 50/100 = 237.5% of Principal

Compound interest = 237.5 × 12000/100 = 28500

Hence, the compound interest for the first 3 years is Rs. 28500

questions.question: What is that greatest four-digit number which when divided by 3 and 4 leaves remainder 2 in each case?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of divisors (3, 4) = 12.

Largest 4-digit number divisible by 12 is 9996.

Required number = (Largest number divisible by 12) + Remainder.

Required number = 9996 + 2 = 9998.

**∴ The correct answer is 9998.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Divisors = 3 and 4, Remainder in each case = 2.

Formula: Number = [LCM(Divisors) × k] + Remainder.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f537dce4f75253a0ac5a690f64f9b27b23cfa01770d157fe273a5c1fba1ffee7.png] 

⇒ Step 1: Find LCM of 3 and 4.

⇒ LCM(3, 4) = 12.

⇒ Step 2: Divide the greatest 4-digit number (9999) by 12 to find the remainder.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 12 = 833 with a remainder of 3.

⇒ Step 3: Find the greatest 4-digit number exactly divisible by 12.

⇒ 9999 − 3 = 9996.

⇒ Step 4: Add the common remainder 2 to this value.

⇒ 9996 + 2 = 9998.

**∴ The correct answer is 9998.**

**__Additional Information__**

General Form for Same Remainder

Any number that leaves a remainder 'r' when divided by x, y, and z is of the form: [LCM(x, y, z) × k] + r, where k is an integer.

LCM and HCF Relationship

For any two numbers a and b, HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Greatest n-digit Number logic

To find the greatest n-digit number divisible by L, subtract (n-digit max ÷ L)'s remainder from the n-digit max value.</p

questions.question: A number is first increased by 12% and then decreased by 12%. The change in number is:
questions.solution:

A number is first increased by 12% and then decreased by 12%

**Concept:**

Successive percentage changes can be calculated by a + b + ab/100 formula.

**Solution:**

**Hence, the change in number is 1.44% decrease (Option 4).**

questions.question: A person bought an article and sold it at a loss of 10 percent. If he had boughs it for 30 percent less price and sold it for Rs. 90 more, then he would earn a profit of 35 percent. What is the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

Initial Selling Price (SP) at 10% loss = 100 − 10 = 90 units.

New CP at 30% less price = 100 − 30 = 70 units.

New SP at 35% profit on the New CP = 70 + (35% of 70) = 70 + 24.5 = 94.5 units.

Difference in SP = 94.5 − 90 = 4.5 units ⇒ 4.5 units = Rs. 90 ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 20 ⇒ 100 units = Rs. 2000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial loss percentage = 10%

New cost price is 30% less than the initial cost price.

New selling price is Rs. 90 more than the initial selling price.

New profit percentage = 35%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e5f7baf8093748285e5c0be0140eaa4d11082494bfc78234cb5bab83da01561.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the initial Cost Price (CP) be x.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP) = x − (10% of x) = 0.9x

⇒ New Cost Price (CP) = x − (30% of x) = 0.7x

⇒ New Selling Price (SP) = 0.7x + (35% of 0.7x)

⇒ New SP = 0.7x × 1.35 = 0.945x

According to the given condition, New SP is Rs. 90 more than the Initial SP:

⇒ 0.945x − 0.9x = 90

⇒ 0.045x = 90

⇒ x = 90 ÷ 0.045

⇒ x = 2000

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when SP > CP (Profit = SP − CP). Loss occurs when CP > SP (Loss = CP − SP). Both profit and loss percentages are strictly calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount percentage is computed as (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price

Discount is always applied directly on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. Selling Price (SP) is obtained as SP = MP − Discount.
</p

questions.question: If p ∶ q ∶ r = 2 ∶ 5 ∶ 3 and r ∶ s = 6 ∶ 5, then what is the value of p ∶ q ∶ r ∶ s?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

p ∶ q ∶ r = 2 ∶ 5 ∶ 3

r ∶ s = 6 ∶ 5

Find p ∶ q ∶ r ∶ s

**Concept:**

The ratio p ∶ q ∶ r can be joined with the ratio r ∶ s when the common term r is the same in both.

**Solution:**

Make r the same in both ratios by multiplying p ∶ q ∶ r by 2 and r ∶ s by 1:

⇒ 2(2 ∶ 5 ∶ 3) ∶ 1(6 ∶ 5)

⇒ 4 ∶ 10 ∶ 6 ∶ 5

Simplifying we get 4 ∶ 10 ∶ 6 ∶ 5

**Hence, p : q : r : s = 4 : 10 : 6 : 5 (Option 2).**

questions.question: What is the smallest integer that is divisible by 12, 22 and 32?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The smallest integer divisible by the given numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

Numbers: 12, 22, 32

Take the largest number 32. To be divisible by 12 (4 × 3), it needs a factor of 3.

To be divisible by 22 (2 × 11), it needs a factor of 11.

LCM = 32 × 3 × 11 = 1056

**∴ The correct answer is 1056.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 12, 22 and 32.

**Formula Used:**

The smallest integer exactly divisible by a set of numbers is their Least Common Multiple (LCM).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factorization of 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 22 = 2¹ × 11

⇒ Prime factorization of 32 = 2⁵

⇒ The LCM is the product of the highest power of each prime factor involved.

⇒ LCM = 2⁵ × 3¹ × 11¹

⇒ LCM = 32 × 3 × 11

⇒ LCM = 96 × 11 = 1056

**∴ The correct answer is 1056.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

It is the smallest positive integer that is perfectly divisible by each of the given numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

It is the largest positive integer that divides each of the given numbers without leaving a remainder.

Product Rule of Two Numbers

For any two numbers a and b: LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b) = a × b

LCM of Fractions

LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)
</p

questions.question: Find the area of the rhombus whose diagonals are 16 cm and 20 cm.
questions.solution:
Given:

Diagonal 1 (d1) = 16 cm

Diagonal 2 (d2) = 20 cm

Find area of rhombus

**Concept:**

Area of a rhombus = 0.5 × d1 × d2

**Solution:**

Area = 0.5 × d1 × d2 = 0.5 × 16 × 20 = 160 cm²

**Hence, the area of the rhombus is 160 cm² (Option 3).**

questions.question: A train moves at a speed of 30 m/s and crosses a bridge of length 650 metres in 50 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
Given:

Train speed = 30 m/s

Bridge length = 650 m

Time to cross = 50 s

**Concept:**

The total distance covered when a train crosses a bridge is the sum of the length of the train and the length of the bridge. This total distance is equal to the speed of the train times the time it takes to cross the bridge.

**Solution:**

Total distance covered = speed × time = 30 × 50 = 1500 m

Length of train = total distance - bridge length = 1500 - 650 = 850 m

**Hence, the length of the train is 850 metres (Option 3).**

questions.question: Asha bought a saree for Rs. 4000 and sold it for Rs. 4400. Her profit percent is:
questions.solution:
Given:

CP = Rs. 4000

SP = Rs. 4400

Find profit percent

**Concept:** Profit percent = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100%

**Solution:**

Profit = SP - CP = 4400 - 4000 = Rs. 400

Profit percent = (Profit/CP) × 100% = (400/4000) × 100% = 10%

**Hence, her profit percent is 10%.**
